models.collectorNote: A Full Classic under CCCA rules, with values to match. Custom-bodied Twelves sit at the top; series production sedans are the (relative) entry ticket to V12 Packard ownership.

generations.name: Twelve (V12)
generations.note: The 7.3-litre V12 made 160 hp with a refinement nothing at the price matched. Dietrich and LeBaron bodies on the long wheelbases are the blue-chip cars of the Classic era.

models.intro: Packard's V12 flagship — launched as the Twin Six in 1932, renamed Twelve a year later — was Detroit's answer to the great European chassis: silent, torquey, and bodied by the best shops in America.
models.name: Twelve

generations.name: Super Eight
generations.note: Engines grew from 5.2 to 5.8 litres across the run and the 1940s One-Sixty flagship trim shared the line. Postwar Super Eights and Super Clippers carried the marque until the V8 era.

models.intro: The straight-eight backbone of the Packard range for nearly two decades — the car most people meant by 'a Packard' — spanning the Classic era, the streamline years and the first postwar cars.
models.name: Super Eight

models.collectorNote: The most collectible postwar Packard. Convertibles lead, the one-year hardtop is the connoisseur's pick, and original tri-tone schemes documented from the build sheet matter.

generations.name: Caribbean
generations.note: The 1955 cars brought Packard's new V8 and torsion-level suspension; the 1956 Caribbean's 6.1-litre V8 made 310 hp, the strongest Packard ever built. Production was in the hundreds per year.

models.intro: Packard's halo car of the fifties: a low-volume convertible with continental flair, wire wheels and tri-tone paint, built to fight Cadillac's Eldorado. The 1956 hardtop joined for the final year.
models.name: Caribbean

models.collectorNote: Rarity plus the end-of-story significance keeps Hawks wanted. The supercharger and its health are the inspection's first item.

generations.name: Packard Hawk
generations.note: Just 588 were built. Under the fibreglass nose sat Studebaker's supercharged 289 V8 at 275 hp — the fastest car wearing a Packard badge that year, and a poignant full stop.

models.intro: The last real Packard, built for one year on Studebaker bones in South Bend: a supercharged Golden Hawk in Packard dress, with padded armrests on the outside of the doors and the marque's final flourish of fins.
models.name: Hawk
